title: Molecular Docking and Functional Analyses Reveal the Chondroprotective and Anti-Inflammatory Potential of Statins in Osteoarthritis.
authors: Kilinc, Bugrahan Regaip; Kostak, Feyza; Yilmaz, Omer Faruk; Pehlivanoglu, Suray; Sirin, Duygu Yasar
journal: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine
one_liner_zh: 该研究用分子对接评估他汀类药物与NF-kB、IL-1beta等蛋白的结合，但对象是蛋白-小分子而非蛋白-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，仅边缘相关。
abstract: Osteoarthritis is a progressive degenerative joint disorder characterised by cartilage degradation and chronic inflammation. Beyond their well-established lipid-lowering properties, statins, particularly pitavastatin and rosuvastatin, have demonstrated promising anti-inflammatory and chondroprotective effects. This study comprehensively evaluated these effects on human primary chondrocytes using an integrative approach involving in silico and in vitro experiments. Key molecular targets, including NF-kappaB, IL-1beta and SOX9, were analysed to elucidate the mechanisms underlying the therapeutic potential of these statins. Molecular docking analyses using the CB-Dock2 platform revealed strong binding affinities of both statins with the target proteins, with pitavastatin exhibiting a higher binding score (-8.0) compared to rosuvastatin (-7.9). Bioinformatics analyses via STITCH and STRING databases highlighted the involvement of both statins in pathways regulating inflammation, lipid metabolism, and cartilage homeostasis. In vitro experiments demonstrated that both statins preserved chondrocyte viability at 24 and 48 h; however, prolonged exposure led to significant declines, with rosuvastatin exhibiting greater cytotoxicity. Western blot analyses confirmed that both statins effectively suppressed IL-1beta expression, indicative of potent anti-inflammatory activity. Pitavastatin transiently enhanced SOX9 expression, peaking at 24 h before declining, while rosuvastatin showed a more sustained but moderate increase. NF-kappaB expression steadily increased over time with both statins, suggesting potential activation of compensatory inflammatory pathways during prolonged exposure. These findings underscore the dual anti-inflammatory and chondroprotective roles of pitavastatin and rosuvastatin, while highlighting the need for careful consideration of dosage and treatment duration to mitigate cytotoxic effects and provide novel insights into the molecular mechanisms of statins.
abstract_zh: 骨关节炎是一种以软骨退化和慢性炎症为特征的进行性退行性关节疾病。除其公认的降脂特性外，他汀类药物，尤其是匹伐他汀和瑞舒伐他汀，已展现出有前景的抗炎和软骨保护作用。本研究采用整合方法，结合计算机模拟 (in silico) 和体外 (in vitro) 实验，全面评估了这些药物对人原代软骨细胞的影响。分析了关键分子靶点，包括NF-kappaB、IL-1beta和SOX9，以阐明这些他汀类药物治疗潜力的潜在机制。使用CB-Dock2平台进行的分子对接 (molecular docking) 分析显示，两种他汀类药物与靶蛋白均具有强结合亲和力，其中匹伐他汀的结合评分（-8.0）高于瑞舒伐他汀（-7.9）。通过STITCH和STRING数据库进行的生物信息学 (bioinformatics) 分析强调了两种他汀类药物在调节炎症、脂质代谢和软骨稳态通路中的参与。体外实验表明，两种他汀类药物在24和48小时时均保持了软骨细胞活力；然而，长时间暴露导致显著下降，其中瑞舒伐他汀表现出更大的细胞毒性。Western blot分析证实，两种他汀类药物均有效抑制IL-1beta表达，表明其具有强效抗炎活性。匹伐他汀短暂增强SOX9表达，在24小时达到峰值后下降，而瑞舒伐他汀则表现出更持续但适度的增加。两种他汀类药物处理下，NF-kappaB表达随时间稳步增加，提示长时间暴露期间可能存在代偿性炎症通路的激活。这些发现强调了匹伐他汀和瑞舒伐他汀的双重抗炎和软骨保护作用，同时突出了需谨慎考虑剂量和治疗持续时间以减轻细胞毒性，并为他汀类药物的分子机制提供了新见解。
